reason: The hypothesis relies on Cu surface segregation as the key premise, but the only cited supporting evidence (E1) reports Cu segregation in as-synthesized CrFeCoNiCu nanoparticles at room temperature, not thermally induced segregation in FeNiCrCoCu. The conflicting evidence (E2) explicitly rules out surface segregation in a similar HEA system. The lower melting point of Cu is textbook knowledge, but the specific claims about thermally driven segregation, quasi-liquid layer formation, and its role in melting progression lack direct prior evidence.
premises: Cu has a lower melting point than the other constituent metals in FeNiCrCoCu
Cu segregates to the surface of FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles upon heating
The segregated Cu forms a quasi-liquid layer at sub-bulk-melting temperatures
This quasi-liquid layer facilitates progressive melting into the core
